# OpenSocrates 1.1.5

OpenSocrates 1.1.5 fixes three issues found during a clean-install deep review:
Claude grounding under default permissions, honest Codex hook-trust guidance,
and real installed-package integrity diagnosis.

## Highlights

- Claude grounding files now prefer a private `.opensocrates` area inside the
  active workspace. Claude can read them without `--add-dir`, the area is
  invisible to `git status`, and OS-temp fallback plus cross-root cleanup keep
  read-only or upgrade scenarios fail-open.
- `diagnose` now hashes the complete installed package against
  `checksums.sha256` and validates the release manifest's version, host, and
  content revision. It reports explicit mismatch or unavailable states instead
  of treating file presence as verification.
- The installer and Codex package README explain the required one-time
  interactive hook approval. Until approval, non-interactive `codex exec` may
  silently skip the untrusted hooks.
- Release tests cover workspace placement, fallback, cross-root receipts and
  cleanup, Git invisibility, intact packaged runtimes, and staged package
  tampering.

## Upgrade notes

Update both managed hosts together with:

```bash
npx --yes opensocrates@1.1.5 update --host all
```

After the Codex update, open one interactive Codex session and approve the
OpenSocrates hooks before relying on automatic selection. The released native
package remains limited to Apple-silicon macOS (`darwin-arm64`). Package
checksums detect local change or damage but are not a signed authenticity proof.

OpenSocrates still retains no raw prompts, transcripts, credentials, local
paths, hook payloads, tool output, selector reasoning, or user identity.
